issues.summary: IAMAI can store the operator-entered proof date/result, but the drill itself remains interactive human evidence.
If IAMAI cannot distinguish a scheduled drill from an unrelated emergency-account sign-in, it must not infer the drill is complete from sign-in logs alone.

The renderer must supply the exact current unassessed-policy list and exact pinned source objects from IAMAI's already-loaded baseline package. This is a presentation/binding integration of existing baseline truth, not a new tenant read.
If IAMAI does not currently expose the unsupported semantic field/reason per policy, display the policy as unassessed without inventing a reason and preserve the source artifact for human review.
Retained baseline documentation and exported member disagree about administrator exclusion/scope. No implementation is authored until the baseline is corrected/reviewed.
If IAMAI cannot already distinguish whether the Microsoft Intune Enrollment service principal exists, keep resource absence Unknown rather than adding a new tenant read during content integration.
IAMAI must map existing directory evidence to distinguish user-based service accounts from service principals before enforcement. Do not claim user-scoped CA covers service principals.
Workflow-owner/source-network validation remains human evidence when IAMAI has not observed every scheduled or infrequent workflow.

Available project authority defines both valid first-enforcement choices but does not reveal which one the owner selected. Package therefore supports both deterministically and emits no actionable implementation in needsDecision. Do not guess.
IAMAI integration must map its existing guest/external population evidence to an enforcement-safe prerequisite. Do not add a new tenant read solely for this content package.

IAMAI must map its existing MFA-registration, hybrid/password-writeback, and High-risk-policy evidence into prerequisite/readiness bindings. Do not add new tenant reads solely for this content package.
Final library review should confirm the current-API normalization from retained-source authenticationStrength to the v1.0-supported mfa + passwordChange AND grant.

facts: POST /identity/conditionalAccess/policies creates a policy.
PATCH /identity/conditionalAccess/policies/{id} updates a policy.
Policy.Read.All plus Policy.ReadWrite.ConditionalAccess are least delegated permissions for create/update; Conditional Access Administrator and Security Administrator are supported built-in roles.
conditionalAccessPolicy state values include enabled, disabled, enabledForReportingButNotEnforced.
Conditional Access requires Microsoft Entra ID P1; Microsoft 365 Business Premium includes Conditional Access rights.
POST /identity/conditionalAccess/namedLocations creates an ipNamedLocation using #microsoft.graph.ipNamedLocation plus displayName and ipRanges.
PATCH /identity/conditionalAccess/namedLocations/{id} updates an IP named location.
When updating ipRanges, the request must carry every range that should remain; omitted ranges are removed.
Policy.Read.All plus Policy.ReadWrite.ConditionalAccess are least delegated permissions for create/update; Conditional Access Administrator and Security Administrator are supported roles.

technicalPrimitives.surface: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access + Microsoft Graph v1.0
facts: Sign-in frequency supports time-based hour/day controls and persistent-browser mode can be set to never.
The persistent-browser session control should target All apps/resources to work correctly.
Graph v1.0 exposes persistentBrowser, signInFrequency, and deviceFilter shapes used by this package.
The current Graph v1.0 conditionalAccessSessionControls schema does not expose secureSignInSession.
The Graph beta conditionalAccessSessionControls schema exposes secureSignInSession and secureSignInSessionControl.isEnabled.
Microsoft warns Graph beta APIs are subject to change and unsupported for production applications; this is an isolated package exception.

technicalPrimitives.surface: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access + Microsoft Graph v1.0
facts: Conditional Access workload policies must target an eligible service principal directly; assigning a policy to a group containing the service principal does not enforce it.
Use the Enterprise applications service principal Object ID, not the App registrations Object ID.
Location-based workload policy can include All resources, include Any location, exclude the approved named location, and Block access.
Graph v1.0 conditionalAccessClientApplications exposes includeServicePrincipals and excludeServicePrincipals.
Microsoft Entra Workload ID Premium is required to create or modify service-principal Conditional Access policies.
Invoke-MgGraphRequest is in Microsoft.Graph.Authentication and supports REST GET/POST/PATCH; Body is required for POST/PATCH.

technicalPrimitives.surface: Microsoft Entra PIM + Microsoft Graph v1.0
facts: PATCH /identity/conditionalAccess/authenticationContextClassReferences/{id} creates or updates an authentication context and isAvailable publishes it for use.
AuthenticationContext.ReadWrite.All is the least delegated write permission; Conditional Access Administrator and Security Administrator are supported roles.
For PIM activation, Microsoft recommends creating and enabling the matching authentication-context CA policy before selecting the context in PIM.
A matching context CA policy that is Report-only or disabled does not trigger PIM backup MFA.
Every time reauthentication has a documented 10-minute window across activations.
Privileged Identity Management capabilities require an eligible Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance entitlement for users in scope.
PATCH /policies/roleManagementPolicies/{policyId}/rules/{ruleId} updates one PIM rule without replacing unrelated rules.
AuthenticationContext_EndUser_Assignment is the authentication-context activation rule and claimValue stores the authentication-context claim.
RoleManagementPolicy.ReadWrite.Directory is the least delegated write permission for Entra role policy rules; Privileged Role Administrator is the supported least-privileged write role.

validationLimitations: PowerShell AST/parser was unavailable in the authoring container for this authoring run. 40 packages expose PowerShell content; extracted scripts were statically/mechanically checked where package metadata records that check and should be AST-parsed by the implementation environment before use.

219 of 264 global binding definitions were not present in the previous LIBRARY.json registry. Their package usage is captured here, but type/sensitivity/existing-IAMAI mapping must be normalized during the planned whole-library integration review rather than guessed.

implementationCaveats.summary: Microsoft still documents authentication transfer as preview in 2026. The Conditional Access authenticationFlows condition is available in Graph v1.0; the package remains pinned to the retained baseline and uses Report-only validation.

Microsoft documents that authentication-flow policies targeting All resources also affect Device Registration Service, and some Teams devices can depend on device code flow. Legitimate use must be remediated or explicitly resolved before enforcement; this package does not invent an exception absent from the retained baseline.

Microsoft documents a 10-minute reauthentication window across PIM activations after one successful reauthentication. The CA policy is configured for Every time, but the product must not promise a literal new prompt on every activation.

Microsoft states that from July 6, 2026 Register security information Conditional Access also applies during Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO credential registration. Report-only validation must include those workflows where present.

The retained raw/goalMap projection does not expose a dedicated stable member for this goal. IAMAI does expose explicit canonical step/goal semantics. This package does not invent a source GUID; create uses the resolved target and correction requires the stable tenant policy ID.

IAMAI source calls for a 3-day Mark device non-compliant grace action in each applicable compliance policy. This package does not blind-bulk-edit unknown Intune policy IDs; the prerequisite must be resolved against the tenant compliance-policy set.
Intune compliance configuration is not contained in Conditional Access JSON. The CA policy is only actionable when IAMAI says the compliance prerequisite is real for the in-scope platforms.

IAMAI’s canonical merged-step source specifies the unmanaged-device companion policy, but the available pinned projection does not surface a stable source-member ID for that companion. No source GUID is invented; tenant updates require IAMAI’s resolved stable tenant policy ID.

As checked on 2026-09-10, secureSignInSession is exposed by conditionalAccessSessionControls in Graph beta but not in the v1.0 resource schema. The portal feature is supported; JSON/PowerShell mutation for this field therefore uses an isolated beta endpoint.

Token Protection is supported in the Entra portal, but secureSignInSession is not exposed in the current Graph v1.0 session-control schema. JSON/PowerShell mutation is isolated to Graph beta and must be reverified before production integration.

Policy B uses Conditional Access App Control / cloudAppSecurity blockDownloads and requires the Defender for Cloud Apps dependency. If unavailable, Policy A can still be authored but Policy B is not silently omitted from completion truth.

Microsoft documents that choosing Allow limited, web-only access on the SharePoint unmanaged-devices page disables previous Conditional Access policies created from that page and creates a new all-users CA policy; customizations are not carried over. IAMAI must stop and rescan after this prerequisite change before mutating CA by stable ID.
Per-user MFA strongAuthenticationRequirements is currently exposed through the beta authentication requirements API; no v1.0 equivalent is documented.
implementationCaveats.scope: Only explicit per-user MFA read/update operations in this package; do not generalize beta use.

generationNotes: Rebuilt from the 46 authored V2.5 compact package META.json/CONTENT.md sources available in this authoring run.
Package rows, output eligibility, state projections, binding usage, source counts, issues, and block counts are derived from package metadata/content rather than reconstructed from memory.

The global binding registry preserves definitions from the previous LIBRARY.json where they existed; newly encountered bindings are intentionally marked pending holistic integration review instead of inventing types or IAMAI mappings.
Shared technical primitive definitions are preserved from the previous LIBRARY.json and package membership is expanded only from explicit sharedTechnicalPrimitives declarations.

bindingRegistryPolicy.canonicalVocabulary: Binding names are the union declared by package META.json files.
bindingRegistryPolicy.newDefinitions: Bindings absent from the previous global registry are not guessed; they remain pending type/sensitivity/existing-IAMAI mapping review.
bindingRegistryPolicy.integrationBoundary: A pending binding definition is not permission to add a tenant read or new reasoning. Integration must map it to existing IAMAI facts or report a genuine gap.
